currentContext.business: As a standalone entity RPSG Ventures is a focused IT solutions provider to Group companies in the power generation and distribution sector, offering IT consultancy, project management and software development designed for the operational and regulatory requirements of the power sector. Along with its subsidiaries it operates across business process management, FMCG including ayurvedic and wellness products, real estate and sports, and it also invests in and incubates new opportunities through venture capital participation and direct investments in emerging brands. Its customer base at the standalone level is largely comprised of internal Group entities, a captive customer model that supports strong integration and faster implementation cycles.

IT Services: IT Network & Infrastructure - Setup, Operations and Maintenance (O&M)
Data Centre and Disaster Recovery solutions
Cyber Security Solutions, Operations and Governance
Business Process Management: Firstsource Solutions Limited (FSL) - intelligent enterprise operations under the 'Intelligence That Operates' model
Real Estate: Multi-phase residential project at Haldia, West Bengal
Sports: Lucknow Super Giants (LSG) - Indian Premier League
Durban's Super Giants (DSG) - South Africa T20 League (SA20)
Mohun Bagan Super Giant (MBSG) - Indian Super League

currentContext.expansion: RPSG Ventures is an asset-light services business at the standalone level, so its expansion during 2025-26 was a platform and footprint build-out rather than plant capacity. On the IT side the Company migrated all applications to a modern private cloud environment based on hyper-converged infrastructure technology and set up a Disaster Recovery (DR) site in a different seismic zone at Greater Noida, Uttar Pradesh, strengthening business continuity and systems availability. Under the process re-engineering initiative Project Drishti it implemented the CESC Generation Data Lake, consolidating data from the three generating stations at Budge Budge, Haldia and Chandrapur across fuel management, generation performance, ash management, operations & maintenance and asset health, and modified Generation-division applications to ensure readiness for integration with the planned ERP implementation. Other builds included a safety incident and observation management system, a biometric-enabled timesheet system for Budge Budge Generating Station, a workflow-driven purchase approval application, net metering / net billing / gross metering systems for rooftop solar consumers of CESC, a web application for the Asia Institute of Power Management, a Single Sign-On portal and a new Bill Revision module for the Malegaon Distribution Franchise, and tariff-order and billing/CRM upgrades for the Rajasthan Distribution Franchises. Group footprint expansion came through the corporate structure: Manchester Originals Limited, Jaye Inc. d/b/a TeleMedik, Firstsource Solutions Canada Inc., Pastdue Credit Solutions Limited and Firstsource Middle East Services LLC became subsidiaries during the year, FSP Design Private Limited and FSP International Inc. became associates, and after the year-end the Company incorporated a wholly owned subsidiary, RPSG Brands Mena Private Limited, on April 21, 2026; Bowlopedia Restaurants India Limited was voluntarily liquidated and obtained its dissolution order from the NCLT on May 13, 2026. In the consumer businesses, Guiltfree Industries expanded its product portfolio across packaged snacks and personal care, expanded distribution reach through quick commerce platforms and made its foray into international markets, while Herbolab operates an AYUSH-approved, GMP-certified manufacturing facility in Silvassa alongside an R&D centre in Thane. In real estate, Quest Properties manages Kolkata's first luxury shopping mall 'Quest' and is developing a residential project in Haldia, West Bengal. The Board did not recommend a dividend in order to conserve resources and strengthen the Company's financial position for future growth and expansion.

risks.note: The war in the Middle East has created considerable uncertainties that significantly affect the macroeconomic outlook, especially for emerging market economies, and will result in moderation in Indian economic activity in 2026-27 as already noted by the RBI. Management believes the impact is contained given the size of its operations, reasonable debt exposure at the standalone level and no direct exposure to foreign currency movements.

risks.risk: Dependence on the health of the power sector
risks.note: The Company's services are primarily aimed at the power sector, so its fortunes are closely tied to that sector; any deterioration in the power-sector outlook can affect the Company through rationalisation of IT projects and spends. Management's mitigant is that demand for electricity, being an essential service, should remain relatively insulated even if the economic environment worsens.

A key operational risk is reliance on a limited number of clients and sectors - the standalone customer base is largely comprised of internal Group entities and exports contribute nil of turnover. The Company strives to expand its client base beyond the Group as well as beyond the power sector in the future.
Keeping up with technology and related advancements is required to stay competitive; the risk is addressed through a well-structured framework that assigns ownership to monitor and mitigate risks.

The Company must attract and retain talent and ensure adequate employee utilisation to maintain profitability. Permanent-employee turnover rose to 15.64% in FY 2025-26 from 8.27% in FY 2024-25. Management believes its HR policies and processes effectively mitigate some of the employee related risks.

risks.risk: Regulatory and contractual compliance, including data privacy and IT security
risks.note: The Company is subject to data privacy laws and related rules and regulations that could have a material adverse effect on the business, and is also subject to labour laws. Operational risk also includes possible failure to comply with laws and regulations or to successfully meet contractual obligations including IT security and related services, leading to fines, penalties and lengthy litigations.

risks.risk: Execution risk on the Quest mall refresh while the asset remains operational
risks.note: The brand-mix optimisation and fascia/common-area upgrade is being implemented while the mall stays open, so activities have been staggered over a completion timeline of about one year. It depresses rental revenue as concessions are provided judiciously to certain brands; footfalls declined 31% in 2025-26 although the decline in aggregate annual mall turnover was limited to 3%.

risks.risk: Governance change in the football league in which Mohun Bagan Super Giant participates
risks.note: Following the expiration of the Master Right Agreement (MRA) with Football Sports Development Limited (FSDL), the Indian Super League is being managed by a joint effort involving AIFF and participating clubs, and the 2025-26 season only started on 14th February 2026.

themes.title: AI-led IT services & ER&D transformation
themes.need: Q1FY27 split the bucket three ways: a soft large-cap core, a re-accelerating mid-cap tier, and an outright business-model change. TCS grew constant currency only +0.4% QoQ / +3.2% YoY despite $9.5bn of TCV (including an ~$800mn net-new SKF mega-deal), and its AI-services book annualising $2.6bn (+13.6% QoQ) saw incremental adds DECELERATE from +$125mn to +$75mn - AI is still project revenue, not annuity. WIPRO is the laggard (+0.9% YoY cc, margin -120bps to 16.0%, Q2 guided -1.5% to +0.5%). Mid-caps are outgrowing: TECHM grew +6.6% YoY cc with every vertical up and an 11th consecutive quarter of margin expansion (14.4%, +330bps); MPHASIS's pipeline is at an all-time high, 2.8x its size at the Mphasis.ai launch and +28% YoY, with AI-led deals now 70% of it (from 12%) and BFS pipeline +100% YoY, and its new Tria platform closed multiple opportunities within seven weeks of launch; FRACTAL lifted net income +92% YoY on INR 912.5cr revenue at NRR 117% with zero churn (though only +9% cc, dragged by TMT -22%); KPITTECH won $349M of new deals with 21% of pipeline now productized AI/SDV solutions. Structurally, HCLTECH is entering the AI-datacenter business with an initial investment of up to INR 3,500cr and a 50MW long-term ambition, and PERSISTENT is buying Nagarro at EUR 1.27bn EV to build a $2.9bn / 46,000-person group - European scale is now bought, not built. The new cost line is visas: TATAELXSI crossed INR 1,000cr of quarterly revenue for the first time (INR 1,021.1cr) yet EBIT fell 330bps QoQ, with 220-230bps of it onsite/subcontractor investment the CFO said cannot be passed to customers.
themes.driver: MPHASIS's guide that 'Q2 is positioned to deliver the best sequential constant currency growth we have delivered in three years' is the most falsifiable claim in the sector; then HCLTECH's AI-datacenter build, the PERSISTENT-Nagarro close, and whether TCS's AI incremental adds re-accelerate off +$75mn.
